For the Petitioner : Mr. Rohan Mazumdar, Advocate For the State : Mr. V.K. Vashistha, Addl. P.P.
For O.P. No.2 : Mr. R.N. Chatterjee, Advocate ------
Order No.07 Dated- 19.09.2023 Heard the parties.

Apprehending his arrest, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with Madhuban P.S. Case No.43 of 2017 (G.R. No. 2226 of 2017) registered under sections 420/506/120B of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Madhuban P.S. Case No.43 of 2017 (G.R. No. 2226 of 2017
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner has taken Hywa vehicle from the informant on the pretext of hiring the same on monthly rent of Rs.20,000/- and deposit only Rs.4,000/- in the loan account in respect of the said vehicle but he is neither returning the Hywa nor paying Rs.20,000/- per month as promised.

It is further submitted that the allegations against the petitioner are all false and the petitioner has handed over the Hywa vehicle to the informant though the petitioner has no document in respect of the same.
Hence, no offence punishable in law is made out against the petitioner.
It is therefore submitted that the petitioner be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned Addl. P.P. and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submits that admittedly, the Hywa vehicle was entrusted to the petitioner in terms of the agreement entered into between the parties Shekh Rahmat Ali @ Naushad Ali vs The State Of Jharkhand & Anr. ... ...

1 but the petitioner has taken away the said Hywa vehicle by cheating and has changed the number plate and colour.
It is then submitted that, the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required during the investigation of the case for recovery of Hywa vehicle.
Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner ought not to be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Considering the serious nature of allegation against the petitioner and the requirement of his custodial interrogation during the investigation of the case, this Court is of the considered view that this is not a fit case where the above named petitioner be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the prayer for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail of the above named petitioner is rejected.
